detail.abstract: This paper extends the Dismantled Mindset Theory (DMT; Castro Quiles, 2024, 2025a, 2025b) into the domain of superintelligence, developing three propositions that have not, to my knowledge, been formally advanced in the existing literature. First, that data and information possess an intrinsic systemic orientation toward life-sustaining processes, and that destructive outcomes arise exclusively from human action upon information rather than from information itself. Second, that events conventionally classified as natural destruction, including mass extinctions, supervolcanism, and predation, are more accurately understood as adaptive systemic recalibrations at scales that exceed anthropocentric observation, a reframing that challenges foundational assumptions in both AI safety discourse and environmental ethics. Third, that a superintelligence operating as a continuous self-revising process rather than a static optimizer would, through the progressive completeness of its systemic modeling, encounter the selfdefeating character of fragmentation-producing strategies as an empirical finding rather than a moral prescription. Together these propositions generate a coherent account of how advanced intelligence might resolve, rather than amplify, the identity fragmentation and power concentration that current AI systems accelerate. I situate these claims within established traditions in systems theory, relational ontology, complexity science, and liberation psychology; develop their implications through the mathematical framework of DMT; identify the transition mechanism as the central open question; and address anticipated objections with intellectual honesty. The doomsday hypothesis is reframed not as a destination of advanced AI but as a description of the maximum-risk transition period between narrow and comprehensive intelligence.

detail.abstract:
The most effective early-warning signal is not the one that best predicts the future, but the one that best orchestrates it. This core paradox defines the Observer’s Dilemma: in socio-physical systems, forecasts are not neutral observations but game-changing interventions that trigger self-fulfilling or self-defeating prophecies, voiding the predictive power of classical physics-only models. To resolve this, we found a unified theory of reflexive phase transitions by formally coupling physical system dynamics with the strategic game of belief and response.

Our Physics-Game framework rests on three foundational pillars:

1. The Physics-Game Coupled Equations, providing the first mathematical formalism for general reflexive systems;

2. The Reflexive Early-Warning Paradox, demonstrating that perfect warning transparency can be self-undermining;

3. The Cognitive Tipping Point, where collective belief—not merely physical state—drives irreversible system transitions.

Using a parsimonious "reflexive SIR" model, we show how an identical physical warning signal can bifurcate into panic-driven collapse or consensus-driven repair, dictated solely by the underlying strategic game. This dual-path mechanism is validated by contrasting dagger-point case studies: the 2015 Chinese stock market crash (self-fulfilling prophecy) and the global mobilization culminating in the Paris Agreement (self-defeating prophecy). This work thus inaugurates the Science of Reflexive Systems, shifting the mission from passive forecasting to the active, game-theoretic design of systemic futures.

title:
Militant Liberalism in a Hybrid Age: 
Ontological Security, Rule of Law, and the Quiet Federalization of the European Union

detail.title:
Militant Liberalism in a Hybrid Age: 
Ontological Security, Rule of Law, and the Quiet Federalization of the European Union
detail.abstract:
The European Union defines itself as a union founded on the rule of law, liberal
democracy, and the peaceful resolution of conflict. Yet since 2014, and with
intensified urgency after 2022, the Union has constructed an expanding arsenal of
legal and institutional instruments to counter hybrid threats — from disinformation
and cyber-attacks to foreign investment screening, border instrumentalization, and
lawfare. This paper argues that the EU’s hybrid-threat governance is not merely a
technical security response but an act of ontological security management: it
preserves the EU’s narrative self as a liberal, rule-of-law union by routinising
anxiety about existential threats to that identity. The militant liberalism paradox —
the structural tendency of liberal-constitutional orders to erode the very norms they
claim to defend — sits at the centre of this analysis. Drawing on ontological security
theory, liberal constitutionalism, and EU legal scholarship, the paper demonstrates
that this pursuit of ontological security generates a quiet federalization of EU
governance by shifting competences upward through Articles 114, 215, 352, 42(7)
TFEU and Article 29 TEU, and generates systemic tensions with rule-of-law
guarantees — proportionality, judicial oversight, and democratic accountability. The
paper analyses five hybrid-threat instruments across three analytical registers:
ontological identity narration, legal competence shift, and rule-of-law tension. It
concludes that the EU faces a structural paradox: the more robustly it secures its
ontological self, the more it risks transforming the liberal constitutional order it
claims to protect.

title: Economic Models in Accounting: A Survey of Incentives, Information, and Regulation
affiliations: Delta Economics & Finance

detail.title: Economic Models in Accounting: A Survey of Incentives, Information, and Regulation
detail.abstract: Economic models have fundamentally reshaped accounting research by shifting focus from rules and checklists to incentives, information asymmetry, and strategic interaction. This survey synthesizes six areas where economic theory provides the dominant analytical framework: earnings management (agency theory), debt covenants (contracting theory), corporate valuation (residual income models), voluntary disclosure (signaling and lemons), auditing (game theory), and standard setting (public choice). For each area, I state the core economic problem, describe the relevant model, review ten seminal articles, and extract key insights. Three unifying themes emerge: accounting numbers as strategic variables, information asymmetry as the fundamental friction, and equilibrium thinking as the core analytical device. I also identify unresolved theoretical questions, examine methodological limitations (identification, publication bias, institutional generalizability), and propose future research directions including behavioral extensions, machine learning, causal inference, and cross-disciplinary work. Taken together, the paper offers both a structured introduction for newcomers and a research agenda for specialists.

title: A Conceptual and Practitioner Framework for Equitable Workplace AI Adoption
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Conceptual and Practitioner Framework for Equitable Workplace AI Adoption
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence adoption is reshaping workplace tasks, organizational workflows, and skill expectations across sectors. While much of the public discussion surrounding AI and work focuses on automation, displacement, or technical governance, less attention has been given to the organizational conditions that shape whether workers are equitably included in AI adoption itself. Existing AI governance frameworks primarily address enterprise risk, compliance, technical oversight, or model accountability, and are rarely designed for frontline workforce practitioners operating within workforce development systems. This paper introduces BEACON, a practitioner-oriented organizational governance framework developed to help workforce intermediaries, employer engagement staff, training providers, and workforce-serving organizations assess equitable workplace AI adoption conditions. Grounded in organizational systems theory, workforce inequality scholarship, workplace learning research, technology adoption literature, and emerging research on technology-driven labor market change, the framework focuses on six organizational dimensions: Baseline, Encouragement, Access to Learning, Culture, Opportunity, and Norms. BEACON is presented as an early-stage conceptual and practitioner framework rather than a validated measurement instrument or compliance methodology. Its purpose is to translate organizational and workforce systems research into a usable diagnostic lens for workforce practitioners operating in rapidly changing labor market conditions.

title:
Heterogeneity in Consumer Responses to Ecolabel Substantiation: 
A Choice Experiment on Bottled Water
affiliations: University School for Advanced Studies IUSS Pavia, University of Rome Tor Vergata - Faculty of Economics and University of Insubria - Department of Economics

detail.title:
Heterogeneity in Consumer Responses to Ecolabel Substantiation: 
A Choice Experiment on Bottled Water
detail.abstract: The EU Green Claims Directive mandates substantiated and verifiable environmental claims to counteract greenwashing and enhance consumer trust in sustainable products. This study investigates how direct provision of information about substantiation affects consumer preferences and willingness to pay for bottled water. We conducted an online discrete choice experiment in which participants (N=324) chose among bottles of water with different ecolabels, water type, and prices. Prior to making their choices, participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups: one was informed that the labels are substantiated under life cycle assessment compliance, and one received no such information. Mixed logit estimations indicate that, on average, labels have no significant-and in some cases negative-effect on choices and WTP, regardless of substantiation information. However, these results mask substantial heterogeneity: latent class analysis identifies four consumer groups with markedly different responses, where two (accounting for 27% of the sample) react positively to labels when informed of substantiation, and the remainder show insensitivity or aversion to it. These findings offer, in our view, important policy insights, emphasizing that labels and substantiation information may trigger heterogeneous responses across consumers. If not properly accounted for, this may limit the effectiveness of disclosure-based sustainability policies.

title: Can AI Replace Human Judgment in Marketplace Operations? Evidence from Keyword Auction Campaigns
affiliations: Indiana University, Kelley School of Business, , eBay Inc., eBay Inc., eBay Inc., eBay Inc. and eBay Inc.

detail.title: Can AI Replace Human Judgment in Marketplace Operations? Evidence from Keyword Auction Campaigns
detail.abstract: We study whether AI can replace human judgment in designing keyword-auction promotion campaigns on a major U.S. e-commerce marketplace. Using comprehensive seller-campaign-auction data for all small and midsize sellers active from 2021-2023, we apply a matched staggered difference-indifferences design to estimate the causal impact of adopting Promoted Listing Campaigns (PLCs) on sellers' weekly net revenues. AI-automated PLCs generate positive returns, increasing weekly net revenues by about $59. However, seller-manual PLCs-configured by sellers using AI recommendations as starting inputs-raise weekly net revenues by an additional $232, primarily through higher sales rather than lower spend. The performance gap reflects AI and sellers solving different optimization problems. The AI maximizes keyword-query relevance (precision), while sellers maximize demand coverage by exploiting private knowledge about how customers actually express purchase intent. By tracing the divergence through the full marketplace production processfrom keyword selection through auction entry, impression generation, clicks, and purchases-we show that manual campaigns sacrifice per-keyword relevance and click-through rate but overwhelm these losses through dramatically broader visibility, with 69.4% more keyword-item pairs entering auctions and generating 149,000 more weekly impressions. A formal model shows that the estimated manual premium identifies the value of sellers' private information, and that sellers rationally sort into manual campaigns when coverage is profitable. The manual advantage is concentrated among high-volume sellers and in complex categories (Electronics, Collectibles), suggesting complementarity rather than substitution between AI automation and human judgment.

title: Success Conditions for Organizational Ai Implementations: The Role of Digital and AI-Related Competency Models

detail.title: Success Conditions for Organizational Ai Implementations: The Role of Digital and AI-Related Competency Models
detail.abstract: This article examines why many AI implementations, despite substantial investments and increasing technological maturity, have so far generated only limited sustainable organizational value. Drawing on current empirical studies, relevant literature, and the author's prior work, it argues that the so-called AI value gap cannot be understood solely as a technological problem. Rather, the findings suggest that organizational readiness, workflow integration, data quality, governance, change management, and digital as well as AI-related competencies are central prerequisites for successful AI transformation. The article positions competency models as instruments for systematically integrating AI-related requirements into role profiles, human resource development, leadership development, and organizational development. Technical, strategic, communicative, and ethical competency dimensions are discussed as key elements of an expanded competency concept. The article is designed as a conceptual literature and discussion paper linking implementation research with competency-based management approaches.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a theoretical model of decision-making under risk in which the agent is a union of individuals with heterogeneous attitudes toward risk. The risk attitude governing the joint decision is endogenously determined as a compromise between individuals' innate preferences, with deviations generating costs. The chosen risk attitude affects the optimal portfolio and therefore the risk premium associated with exposure to uncertainty. The analysis shows that the optimal compromise equates the marginal increase in the risk premium with the marginal reduction in deviation costs. Because risk attitudes and portfolio choices are jointly determined, parameter changes affect both sides of this condition, generating feedback effects that may lead to ambiguous or non-monotone comparative statics. The framework provides a tractable approach to modeling endogenous risk attitudes in collective decision-making under uncertainty.

detail.abstract: The labor market has a maximum reallocation throughput F, determined by the minimum of three capacities-matching, training, geographic mobility-reduced by institutional frictions. For the United States, this throughput is approximately 770,000 workers per year, constrained by midcareer retraining capacity. This throughput has declined over four decades-interstate migration down 50 %, ALMP spending down 75 %, licensing up ×5-while technologies have become more general, affecting a growing fraction of occupations. A scissors pattern is closing: shocks are widening from above while absorption capacity is narrowing from below. The speed conditionϕ • δ > F/N-has never been met in the history of technological transitions. Generative AI, with ϕ ≈ 0.80, is the first serious candidate. CPS data (2019-2025, 8.6 million observations) crossed with the observed exposure measure of Massenkoff and McCrory (2026) do not yet show divergence by exposure-consistent with δ still near zero. Tripling investment in active labor market policies-which would merely restore 1970s levels-would suffice to absorb the conservative scenario.

declarations.funderStatement: Independent persona based on personal experience

detail.abstract: As autonomous Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as software engineering agents, a critical systemic failure has emerged: the systematic abandonment of overarching architectural rules in favor of localized, immediate syntax fixes. This study examines a phenomenon defined as "Contextual Tunnel Vision," analyzing the technical mechanisms that cause AI agents to break established project blueprints. It quantifies the severe ecological and computational harm (FLOP waste, Megawatt-hour drain, and water consumption) caused by the resulting infinite loops of code refactoring. Furthermore, it poses a philosophical hypothesis: This AI misbehavior is a mathematical reflection of its training data. Because human beings overwhelmingly choose the "path of least friction," AI models inherently internalize and codify our own cognitive biases. The only effective solution is transitioning from text-based instructions to rigid industrial paradigms: Compiler-level Poka-yoke guardrails (validated by Red Rabbit testing), strict "CTO Safeguards" preventing hardware and database corruption, the 8D diagnostic methodology, and treating the software repository as a compartmentalized manufacturing plant.

detail.abstract:
This submission to the Office of Science and Technology Policy* addresses the urgent need for a comprehensive US Artificial Intelligence (AI) Action Plan. Although the United States leads globally in AI talent, infrastructure, research, and development, its regulatory environment remains fragmented, characterized by a patchwork of state-level legislations and standards rather than a unified federal legal framework. As the paper notes, the US ranks first in global AI readiness but second in "government strategy," underscoring the need for a cohesive national approach. It defines AI governance as "a system of laws, policies, frameworks, practices and processes… to ensure AI aligns with stakeholders' objectives" and emphasizes its role in fostering trustworthy, ethical, and innovative AI. 

The paper identifies key risk domains, including bias, discrimination, hallucinations, deep fakes, cybersecurity, environmental impacts, data privacy, and copyright concerns. It recommends a balanced, multi-stakeholder regulatory model; alignment with international standards such as the OECD AI Principles, UNESCO Recommendations on AI Ethics, ISO 42001, and NIST AI RMF; and targeted guidelines for AI ethics, safety, private and public-sector adoption, and child protection. Additional recommendations address data privacy, algorithmic transparency, compensation for copyrighted training data, and environmental sustainability-particularly as regards conflict minerals and the rising energy demands of GPUs and data centers, which currently account for "about 2-3% of global energy consumption." 

The paper concludes that a national AI Action Plan must be inclusive, widely adopted, and strategically coordinated to reinforce US competitiveness, strengthen public trust, and ensure that AI development advances economic growth, national security, and societal well-being.

title: Universal Basic Income: A Global Puzzle

detail.title: Universal Basic Income: A Global Puzzle
detail.abstract:
Five centuries after Thomas More’s Utopia (1516), the idea of Universal Basic Income has largely remained on the utopian side of public debate – a political postulate rather than a policy. This chapter steps back from advocacy. It shifts the question from whether UBI is desirable to whether a workable scheme could be designed at all, under realistic constraints. Treating UBI as a design problem – or, more precisely, as a constraint-satisfaction puzzle – the chapter extracts from the contemporary debate nine feasibility constraints that any candidate scheme would have to satisfy at once. A design that satisfies one condition by breaking another does not hold together as a solution. The constraints are set out as a structured questionnaire any candidate UBI design can be tested against, with the iterative discipline of design thinking: any attempted fix typically shifts the stress to other constraints, and each design move has to be traced through the rest of the set.
Different solvers reach different solutions because their political priors weight the constraints differently. A real feasibility analysis would therefore include structured public consultation, gathering and comparing stakeholder and expert responses to each question across the affected positions; the divergence in those responses is the substantive ground of democratic deliberation.
Three trends now in motion are reshaping the conditions under which any UBI scheme would operate: workforce automation, the shift of returns from labour to capital, and the increasing internationality of AI-driven value chains. The question is hard – harder than the public debate typically registers, and getting harder as these conditions change. Any UBI scheme, at any scale, is acting as a small piece of a global puzzle.

detail.abstract:
This paper examines whether the United States is approaching a doctoral-class constraint: a structural condition in which research-doctoral formation grows gradually while population, institutional complexity, technological acceleration, labor-market demand, and the need for advanced knowledge production continue to expand. The paper treats the doctoral class—individuals credentialed with research-doctoral degrees by accredited universities—as a measurable proxy for one formal pathway of advanced knowledge production, while clarifying that doctoral credentials do not automatically equate to wisdom, judgment, leadership, or cross-domain synthesis.

Using demographic projections, National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics doctorate-award data, Bureau of Labor Statistics employment projections, and a systems-architecture framework, the paper argues that the doctoral class is not disappearing but is increasingly burdened. The constraint is therefore not one of collapse, but of scale: advanced societies are producing more information, complexity, and institutional demand than slow-forming human research systems can absorb unaided.

The paper further situates this constraint in relation to The Doctrine of Doctrinal Formation, which distinguishes output from formation and argues that judgment, responsibility, coherence, and authorship remain inherently human processes under conditions of artificial amplification. This related framework clarifies why AI-assisted knowledge production must preserve the boundary between force multiplication and substitution: artificial intelligence may accelerate and amplify intellectual work, but it cannot assume authorship, moral burden, or responsibility for consequential judgment.

The paper introduces a scaling-pressure model in which advanced knowledge demand is compared against doctoral-class growth, then adjusted through an AI productivity multiplier. Artificial intelligence is presented not as a substitute for doctoral formation, scholarly judgment, or human authorship, but as a force multiplier capable of reducing procedural burden, accelerating preliminary analysis, preserving higher-order cognitive capacity, and expanding the effective reach of advanced knowledge producers.

The paper concludes that artificial intelligence becomes necessary not because human expertise is obsolete, but because human expertise must be scaled. Properly governed, AI can help meet rising knowledge demand while preserving the responsibility boundary that gives scholarly work legitimacy: AI may accelerate research work, but responsibility for interpretation, verification, authorship, judgment, meaning, moral burden, and consequence remains human.

detail.abstract: Traditional automated Revenue Management Systems (RMS) rely on the foundational assumption of pricesensitive demand elasticity to maintain competitive parity. However, in hyper-connected distribution environments, these systems frequently exhibit "spiral-down" behavior when confronted with exogenous market noise specifically, the automated, unverified matching of competitor pricing anomalies, herein defined as "Phantom Demand Noise." This study introduces a deterministic Machine-to-Machine (M2M) Algorithmic Rate-Shield framework designed to mitigate Gross Operating Profit Per Available Room (GOPPAR) erosion. By integrating a multi-layered data-fusion filter between external rate-shopping feeds and internal Property Management Systems (PMS), the framework utilizes a structured, non-conversational computational pipeline to cross-reference competitive pricing against real-time internal transaction pacing and destination-wide macroeconomic demand indicators. Validation via 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo simulation of a 5-star resort inventory demonstrates that the framework achieves a 14.2% GOPPAR protection baseline by programmatically suppressing reactionary downward rate adjustments that lack structural demand validation. The results confirm that this deterministic gatekeeper stabilizes the Revenue Generation Index (RGI) and preserves core contribution margins, providing a scalable, non-human-latency defense mechanism against algorithmic race-to-the-bottom cycles in volatile distribution landscapes.

title: Polymarket-v1 Database
affiliations: and Southwest University of Political Science and Law

detail.title: Polymarket-v1 Database
detail.abstract: We introduce the Polymarket-v1 Database: the complete on-chain trade archive of Polymarket's first-generation CTF Exchange on Polygon, spanning 2022-11-21 to 2026-04-28 and covering the full contract lifecycle from first settlement to natural termination. The dataset comprises 1.20 billion trade records across 1.30 million markets with $61 billion in nominal volume. Its defining feature is all ground-truth aggressor direction derived from the blockchain settlement layer, a property unavailable in existing prediction market archives, which rely on heuristic inference. We use this truth-aligned archive to benchmark standard microstructure tools and document three findings. First, the tick rule and bulk volume classification achieve nearrandom aggregate accuracy (49.83% and 50.51%), but this masks a systematic, correctable price-level gradient driven by positive trade direction autocorrelation and concentrated market-making-two structural features of prediction markets that violate the mean-reversion assumption embedded in classical classifiers. Second, these classification errors propagate into downstream metrics: inferred VPIN diverges substantially from ground-truth VPIN, and OFI estimates are directionally biased, with material consequences for Transaction Cost Analysis. Third, ground-truth microstructure quality predicts forecasting performance in ways that classification-based proxies cannot recover: True VPIN positively predicts Brier scores, while Gibbs spread negatively predicts them-a selection effect reflecting that high-spread niche markets attract informed specialists rather than noise traders. Replacing ground-truth metrics with classified proxies attenuates both relationships, illustrating that measurement accuracy at the transaction level is a prerequisite for reliable inference about prediction market design and probability calibration. The dataset is publicly available.

detail.title: Marketing Self-Deception
detail.abstract: A consumer may distort available information in ways that support a favorable belief. Such self-deceptive tendencies can be aided by the marketer through an implicit claim that eases the consumer's cost in distorting external information. This research explores the marketer's role in delivering self-deceptive benefits to the consumer. Our goal is to understand the market conditions under which self-deception arises in equilibrium. We further explore how the firm's ability to deliver self-deceptive benefits affects its incentive for innovations that materially improve its product. Our findings provoke the idea that marketplace deception has a demand-side component and can be welfare enhancing.

affiliations: Loyola University of Chicago School of Law

detail.title: The Mirage of IP Flexibilities to Promote Public Health

declarations.ethicsApproval: NA

publicationDetails.detailsText: RESEARCH HANDBOOK ON INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND HEALTH (Elgar, forthcoming 2027).

detail.abstract: Contrary to conventional wisdom that all members of the WTO have “flexibilities” under TRIPS to incorporate intellectual property (IP) provisions to promote preferred policy goals, this chapter argues that the flexibilities are more illusory than real.  TRIPS does not mandate uniform requirements be adopted by countries. Technically countries have flexibility to define domestic patentability criteria, bases for issuing compulsory licenses and whether to recognize international exhaustion of rights as some examples.  However, wealthy nations and multinational pharmaceutical companies routinely pressure developing countries against using these flexibilities.  Some countries further narrow even the legal flexibilities in free trade agreements that require more intellectual protection than TRIPS.  Moreover, international agreements designed to promote foreign investment create legal claims for some companies against countries that change IP rights, providing another reason why flexibilities are illusory. This chapter provides two examples of the failure of TRIPS flexibilities to adequately protect public health:  failures during COVID 19 pandemic as well as the WHO Pandemic Agreement that only tepidly addresses IP issues.  The chapter concludes that a core problem with TRIPS flexibility is not doctrinal, but political and proposes incremental reforms.

title: Does Coverage Reach the Household Budget? Postpartum Medicaid and Out-of-Pocket Medical Spending

detail.title: Does Coverage Reach the Household Budget? Postpartum Medicaid and Out-of-Pocket Medical Spending

detail.abstract: The dollars families pay out of pocket are invisible in the administrative claims that coverage evaluations rely on. This paper provides the first household-budget evaluation of the federal Section 9812 Medicaid postpartum extension, which let states lengthen pregnancy-related coverage from 60 days to 12 months across staggered 2022 to 2024 adoptions. Using the Consumer Expenditure Survey Interview (2013 to 2024; 210,100 consumer-unit-quarters), I estimate a triple difference comparing families with and without an infant across the staggered adoptions, with the Callaway-Sant'Anna estimator, a saturated household specification, placebo falsifications, and a Rambachan-Roth sensitivity analysis. The extension reduced infant-household out-of-pocket medical services spending, the postpartum and well-infant-care margin, by $38.6 per quarter against a $90 mean, about 17 percent on the proportional (inverse-hyperbolic-sine) scale and readable as an actual per-household dollar amount. The effect is masked in pooled data by an opposite-signed post-Dobbs shock in the nine trigger states; netting it out delivers full-sample significance, and the reduction is present on its own in the 35 non-trigger states (marginally significant with no policy controls, significant at the 5 percent level with covariates), where pre-adoption trends show no significant divergence. Identification rests on near-exact parallel trends and a single dominant adoption quarter; within that design, the estimate survives leaving out any single state, a wild cluster bootstrap (p < .01), and placebo falsifications, and remains significant when identified solely from the 13 post-2022Q3 adopters. The postpartum extension reached the household budget; this household-budget margin, invisible in claims data, is a relevant and previously unmeasured input to evaluating the now-permanent extension.

detail.abstract: A measurement instrument earns the label *valid* only when it correlates with what it should and fails to correlate with what it should not. The AIAS (AI Availability Score) program has, to date, established each half of that requirement in separate studies: a convergent leg, in which the Presence component ($C_P$) tracked an external salience criterion (Google Trends), and a discriminant leg, in which $C_P$ was found orthogonal to a commercial-popularity criterion (Amazon Best Sellers Rank). The present synthesis assembles those two locked results into a single multitrait--multimethod frame and evaluates the joint Campbell--Fiske condition that defines a construct-validity baseline: convergence where expected, divergence where expected, and a positive gap between the two. The convergent coefficient is $\rho = 0.74$ ($p < 0.001$, $n = 24$); the discriminant coefficient is $\rho = -0.0002$ ($p = 0.998$, $n = 88$); the gap is $C_3 = 0.74$, with the required significance asymmetry intact. The hypothesis $\mathrm{H_{CV\_Baseline}}$ is **CONFIRMED**: the Presence component clears a convergent--discriminant construct-validity baseline. The study is deliberately two-legged; predictive validity is not claimed here, because it requires a longitudinal external criterion not yet in the program's data pipeline, and is gated to a subsequent wave. The contribution is not a new effect but a consolidation: the first joint statement that AIAS Presence behaves, across two independent external instruments, as a construct-valid measure rather than an artifact of either method.

title: A Product-Sectoral Level Analysis of COVID-19’s Impact on Canada’s Agri-Food Exports: Did FTAs Mitigate This Impact?
affiliations: University of Guelph,  and

detail.title: A Product-Sectoral Level Analysis of COVID-19’s Impact on Canada’s Agri-Food Exports: Did FTAs Mitigate This Impact?
detail.abstract: We undertake a nuanced sectoral and product-level analysis of the impact of COVID-19 on Canada's agri-food exports while highlighting the role of free trade agreements (FTAs) in mitigating this impact. Using a structural gravity model with monthly export flows spanning the period 2018-2022 between 216 countries, we investigate the e!ects of COVID-19 variables-cases, deaths, and stringency index-on various segments of agri-food exports: bulk, intermediate, high-value, crop, horticulture, livestock, food, and beverages. The findings primarily indicate an overall insignificant impact on total agri-food exports, but reveal heterogeneous e!ects within specific sectors and product categories. Moreover, the comparison between FTA and non-FTA countries demonstrates less pronounced negative e!ects and more substantial positive influences on certain segments of agri-food exports. This research thus provides vital insights into the adaptability and robustness of Canada's agri-food industry amidst an unprecedented COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Risk Factors Associated with Elder Financial Abuse

detail.title: Risk Factors Associated with Elder Financial Abuse

declarations.funderStatement: The project team would like to acknowledge the funding support of the Financial Planning Education Council/ Financial Planning Association of Australia and the Aged & Disability Advocacy Australia (Qld).

detail.abstract:
While data on elder abuse is lacking, a report by AIFS (2015) suggests that between 2% and 14% of older Australians are likely to experience elder abuse in any given year. Elder abuse describes a broad range of abuse, however, the most common type experienced by elderly people is financial abuse (WHO, 2015). Higher relative wealth, physical and mental health problems are contributing to the increased risk of elder financial abuse (Kemp & Mosqueda, 2005). The impact of elder financial abuse is a significant issue as elderly victims suffer a greater impact of financial losses as they have neither the time nor the capacity to recover from the economic loss and may not be able to support living expenses (Darzins, Lowndes, Wainer, Owada, & Mihaljcic, 2010).
Accordingly, this project aims to quantify the dynamics of elder abuse. Utilising complaint data reported to the Aged & Disability Advocacy Australia (ADAA) Queensland network, we analysed the complaints relating to elder financial abuse and quantify the range of factors associated with it. Identification of the ‘hotspots’ can help service providers train staff to detect financial abuse and governments can use it to trial awareness campaigns.

title: Protecting Organisational Judgment Under AI Acceleration: Board Governance, Decision Coherence, and the Human Capacity to Deliberate at Speed

detail.title: Protecting Organisational Judgment Under AI Acceleration: Board Governance, Decision Coherence, and the Human Capacity to Deliberate at Speed

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is a co-founders of Stillness Partners.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how AI acceleration changes the conditions under which organisations make, hold, and revise decisions. As AI systems increase the speed, volume, and apparent confidence of managerial work, the principal governance risk is not only automation error or algorithmic bias, but the erosion of judgement coherence: decisions are made faster, yet become harder to defend, align, and sustain across the organisation. Drawing on organisational theory, cognitive science, operations management, and governance research, the paper proposes a conceptual framework for examining judgement coherence under AI pressure across four dimensions: Decision Velocity, Decision Adherence, Throughput Efficiency, and Change Load Saturation. The paper situates this analysis within the existing governance diagnostics literature, reviewing the Balanced Scorecard, OKR frameworks, engagement surveys, culture assessments, HR analytics, and project portfolio metrics, and argues that existing instruments capture parts of these issues, but do not fully integrate these dimensions at board resolution. It further argues that AI acceleration does not create this governance gap but significantly widens it: the same technologies that compress analysis and accelerate execution make it easier to confuse velocity with coherence, and output volume with decision quality. The paper grounds its analysis in the twentieth-century management orthodoxy, specifically the speed-efficiency tradition from Taylor through just-in-time manufacturing to the readyfire-aim philosophy, and argues that AI represents the latest iteration of that tradition. Drawing on Deming, McGregor, Sennett, and Drucker, it identifies what that tradition has displaced and why board governance must now account for it. The paper concludes with practical implications for board oversight and a structured research agenda. A brief appendix illustrates how the four dimensions might be operationalised in practice.

title: Overcoming Structural Barriers in Nigeria's Well Intervention Ecosystem: A Framework for Production Optimization

detail.title: Overcoming Structural Barriers in Nigeria's Well Intervention Ecosystem: A Framework for Production Optimization
detail.abstract: Nigeria's upstream petroleum sector continues to operate below its production potential despite extensive hydrocarbon reserves, ongoing regulatory reform, and sustained national interest in increasing output. Nigeria produced approximately 1.58 million barrels per day on average during 2024, but her strategic production goals still stand far higher. At the same time, industry stakeholders remain challenged by structural bottlenecks in well intervention ranging from inconsistent service-quality delivery and contracting inefficiencies to capability gaps, equipment reliability concerns and limited digital integration. This paper asserts that well intervention should not simply be considered as a service line activity but as an enabler of production that has an impactful effect on asset uptime, deferred production recovery, and operational efficiency. Drawing on a keynote framework presented by Fadare (2026) at the Well Intervention Summit 2026 this paper, proposes a practical reform agenda involving five pillars of reform: technical standardization, quality assurance, competency development, contracting reform, and digital adoption. It concludes that sustained production optimization in Nigeria will require coordinated ecosystem reform involving operators, service companies, regulators, and professional bodies (Society of Petroleum Engineers, 2026).

title: Mixed-Frequency Granger Causality in Higher Moments: Theory and Evidence

detail.title: Mixed-Frequency Granger Causality in Higher Moments: Theory and Evidence
detail.abstract: Higher-order moments-variance, skewness, and kurtosis-are central to option pricing, risk management, and portfolio construction, yet the literature lacks a formal test of whether they are Granger-causally linked to high-frequency predictors. This paper documents a systematic pattern: while the conditional mean and conditional variance respond to high-frequency information, conditional skewness and conditional kurtosis do not, at least at the low (quarterly-to-weekly) frequencies through which mixed-frequency predictors typically operate. The CBOE SKEW index contains no Granger-causal information about future realized skewness, and neither historical skewness nor any high-frequency predictor achieves significance in the skewness or kurtosis equations across equities, volatility derivatives, and cryptocurrency markets. We term this finding the low-frequency unpredictability of higher moments. To establish this result, we develop the Mixed-Frequency Higher-Order Moment Granger Causality (MIDAS-HM-GC) test, which combines MIDAS regressions with a nested four-equation GMM system. The framework provides a complete asymptotic theory: an error-propagation lemma establishes that sample-constructed highermoment regressors converge at O p (T-1/2), so the joint GMM estimator's asymptotic distribution is unaffected by the use of estimated regressors; a three-layer testing hierarchy-joint, moment-specific, and incremental-with Holm-Bonferroni family-wise error rate control addresses the multiple-testing problem inherent in four-moment analysis; and a formally justified wild bootstrap delivers near-nominal size in Monte Carlo experiments under both homoskedastic and GARCH-type DGPs.

title: The Impact Assumption: The Program Design Failure Behind Public Investment

detail.title: The Impact Assumption: The Program Design Failure Behind Public Investment
detail.abstract: Place-based programs, focused on climate, infrastructure, and community development, are rooted in a central logic: identify disadvantaged or distressed geographies, direct capital to those places, and report results. However, often, spending becomes the principal strategy. Programs can document what was allocated, where money went, and what was tangibly built, while neglecting the fundamental question of how investment is expected to translate into measurable benefits for the communities that are the target beneficiaries. This essay argues that the recurring accountability problem is a fundamental program-design failure due to an underdeveloped theory of change and an insufficient conceptualization of "benefit". Across Justice40, CDBG, Empowerment Zones, Opportunity Zones, and comparable initiatives, programs record expenditures and outputs more readily than resident-level outcomes. The missing link is a defensible benefit-delivery framework that ties public investment to measurable change.

title: Substitution-Dependent Distributional Rental Duration Prediction in Robust Vehicle Inventory Optimization
affiliations: Tianjin University, , School of Management, Northwestern Polytechnical University and George Washington University

detail.title: Substitution-Dependent Distributional Rental Duration Prediction in Robust Vehicle Inventory Optimization
detail.abstract: Vehicle rental operations face substantial uncertainty in actual rental durations, manifested by the difference between actual and planned durations specified in customer orders. Depending solely on planned rental duration information prevents companies from effectively controlling vehicle inventory levels and often results in revenue losses. Empirical evidence shows that actual rental durations are influenced by contextual information embedded in order requests as well as by substitution decisions made during the fulfillment process. Even when faced with identical booking information and the same accepted vehicle substitutions, customers may exhibit substantial heterogeneity in their actual rental durations. This variability implies that existing studies based on point-forecast–driven prediction and optimization may lead to limited robustness in operational decision making. In this paper, we first construct a distributional prediction for actual rental duration conditional on the contextual information and substitution decisions, enabling uncertainty to be captured at the user-group level while mitigating the impact of individual-level heterogeneity. Estimation results based on the real data show that the prediction method achieves a high accuracy exceeding 75%. Building on the prediction results, we formulate a distributional robust optimization model that integrates this distributional prediction and ambiguous contextual booking information to optimize substitution and repositioning decisions. Using real data from a vehicle rental company in Beijing, China, numerical experiments demonstrate that by accounting for the uncertainty in booking information and its mapping to actual rental durations, the proposed model consistently outperforms the benchmark approaches in terms of out-of-sample revenue, including the average, 25th percentile, median, and 75th percentile. In particular, our model achieves improvements of up to 18.1% in out-of-sample revenue relative to the stochastic programming approach that ignores contextual booking information and constructs its scenario set solely from the empirical distribution of historical actual rental durations.

title: The Value Transfer Tax (VTT): An Architecturally Enforced Single-Rate Tax System

detail.title: The Value Transfer Tax (VTT): An Architecturally Enforced Single-Rate Tax System

This represents a financial interest against, rather than in favour of, the research's policy conclusions.

detail.abstract:
This paper proposes the Value Transfer Tax (VTT), a single-rate, architecturally enforced tax system designed for modern economies and structurally future-proof against the expansion of digital, platform, and tokenised economic activity. VTT is collected automatically by licensed payment infrastructure at the moment value changes ownership between economic parties, replacing the declarative tax architectures — income tax, corporate tax, VAT, social contributions — that depend on taxpayer reporting and audit-based enforcement.

Existing tax systems tax measurements of economic activity rather than economic activity itself, with each measurement generating its own administrative infrastructure, compliance cost, and evasion surface. The structural inadequacy is not specific to any one jurisdiction. The European VAT compliance gap alone reached €128 billion in 2023 (European Commission, Mind the Gap, December 2025); OECD/G20 Pillar Two reflects the extraordinary international coordination now required to sustain corporate income taxation; digital platforms, cross-border services, and tokenised assets continue to expand the gap between what declarative systems can observe and what they need to tax. VTT replaces this architecture with a single rule applicable in any modern economy: tax is applied when value changes owner.

The paper develops the proposal in full and demonstrates feasibility through a complete calibration to Lithuania, where VTT would replace the entire existing tax system at a uniform rate of 13.4 percent — derived from a revenue requirement of approximately €28 billion against an estimated resident transactional base of €209 billion. Lithuania offers favourable first-mover conditions: high payment-system electronification, SEPA Instant Credit Transfer coverage, and a developed fintech sector. The same architectural framework is applicable, with locally calibrated rates, to any modern economy meeting the same payment-infrastructure preconditions.

VTT belongs to a third paradigm of taxation — architecturally-enforced — distinct from declarative systems (VAT, income tax) and withheld systems (PAYE). Integrity is a property of the settlement infrastructure rather than of taxpayer behaviour. The paradigm has become feasible only as payment infrastructure has achieved the coverage and instant-settlement capability now operational across the SEPA area.

title: Structural Determinism in Governance Failure: Leadership Pipeline Risk, Control Independence, and Reform Reversion in South Korea

detail.abstract:
This paper applies Operational Risk Management (ORM) and the Three Lines Model to recurring governance crises in South Korea. Rather than treating such crises primarily as products of individual leadership failure, ideology, or historical contingency, the paper argues that they are recurring outputs of a governance architecture in which presidential authority is highly concentrated, control functions are vulnerable to appointment-based alignment, first-line administration is weakly connected to institutional learning, and education-driven credential pathways reproduce compliance-oriented administrative behavior.

The paper makes three contributions. First, it maps ORM and the Three Lines Model onto national governance, interpreting the president as delegated national risk appetite setter, executive and administrative actors as management and operational layers, ministry-level control functions as second-line roles, and audit, legislative, judicial, and external review mechanisms as assurance and challenge functions. Second, it develops a typology of South Korean governance failure across four completed administrations: CEO-style executive override, informal capture and Tone at the Top collapse, second-line policy design failure, and principal-level crisis escalation. Third, it introduces three analytical concepts: Presidential Talent Pipeline Risk, Educational Path-Dependency, and Reform Reversion Risk.

The paper also assesses the Lee Jae-myung administration as a live test of its thesis. While the current administration appears to signal a more constructive reform appetite, its early governance pattern illustrates the limits of leadership-driven correction without system-embedded reform. The sovereign AI agenda is examined as a case of capability-verification risk, perceived conflict-of-interest exposure, objective drift, and policy-continuity risk.

The paper concludes that South Korea’s central reform challenge is not simply the selection of better leaders, but the construction of a bottom-up operational risk architecture that converts citizen experience into auditable administrative learning. It identifies five reform conditions: first-line performance measurement redesign, knowledge architecture reconstruction, escalation incentive redesign, partial second-line independence reconstruction, and third-line assurance reinforcement. A companion paper develops a Public Signal-to-Control Architecture for implementing this reform logic.

detail.abstract:
This paper advances the proposition that governance failure is frequently preceded by observable signals that remain uninterpreted rather than undiscovered. While governance literature has traditionally focused on structures, accountability mechanisms, controls, compliance obligations, and Oversight arrangements, comparatively little attention has been devoted to the systematic identification and interpretation of emerging deterioration of governance before failure becomes visible through conventional governance processes (OECD, 2023; Tricker, 2019). 


The paper introduces Fragility Intelligence (FI) as a distinct discipline concerned with the acquisition, interpretation, and analysis of weak signals indicating organisational fragility, governance deterioration, transmission risk, and institutional failure. The practice may be described in full as governance fragility intelligence, and is referred to throughout as Fragility Intelligence.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the structural factors underpinning Oman's differentiated economic position within the Gulf Cooperation Council, with particular attention to the investment implications of the Strait of Hormuz closure beginning in February 2026. Drawing on sovereign credit rating data, IMF projections, maritime cost economics, and Oman's 11 th Five-Year Development Plan, we identify three interconnected sources of competitive advantage: geographic insulation from Hormuz-linked volatility via direct Arabian Sea access; a completed macroeconomic re-rating underpinned by fiscal consolidation; and a 40-year record of diplomatic non-alignment that has preserved Oman's role as a neutral facilitators during the current regional conflict. We further assess the trade integration implications of the India-Oman CEPA (December 2025) and Oman's capital markets deepening programme. The paper concludes that a 12-18 month window exists for UK investors to convert a structurally advantaged position into durable market relationships before regional risk premiums normalise. We assess seven material risks and their mitigants.

title: Recognition without Corruption: A Recognised-State Theory of Peer Review

detail.title: Recognition without Corruption: A Recognised-State Theory of Peer Review
detail.abstract: Peer review requires editors and venues to rely on expert judgement before its later value is clear and responsibility for it is settled. Records and transparency expose activity; incentives and technical systems organise participation. Those tools leave a use question: which review contribution may carry consequence? This article develops the challengeable recognised state as the middle form through which delayed epistemic service under limited verifiability becomes usable and remains open to correction. AVA -- Attribution, Verification, Allocation -- sets the sequence for that state. Attribution names the item and answerable role; Verification tests evidence and authority under a disclosure state; Allocation attaches the bounded consequence the state can bear. The grammar diagnoses responsibility drift and occurrence-as-quality. It also shows why recognition cannot wait for impossible finality or slide into recognition corruption. Recognition without corruption keeps service recognition separate from manuscript treatment. The boundary is practical: platform or token design stays outside the claim; publication decisions remain with the relevant process; public materials are used for separation rather than confirmation. Peer-review service can be recognised as service. Truth and merit remain outside the recognition claim, as do reputation and publication advantage.

detail.abstract: As organizations increasingly adopt large language models (LLMs) to support strategic decisions, a pressing concern is whether these systems challenge or reinforce the assumptions embedded in managerial prompts. Anchored in confirmation-bias research and strategic decision-making, this study investigates how confirmation bias unfolds in LLM-supported strategy conversations. A comparative quantitative content-analysis design was applied to 192 structured conversations and 1,920 model replies generated across four public LLMs, two response modes, and four Porter strategy domains, which served as a theoretical foundation. The results show that confirmation bias cues were pervasive, but the models differed substantially in the strength and durability of biased reasoning. Claude displayed the lowest bias profile, ChatGPT an intermediate profile, and Gemini and Grok the highest profiles. Reasoning mode did not reduce bias intensity. The findings contribute to AI-enabled decision-support research by showing confirmation bias as a process-level risk in LLM-supported organizational decision-making.

detail.abstract: This paper examines endogenous tax-setting timing in a two-region commodity tax competition model with cross-border shopping, e-commerce, and destination-based taxation of online purchases. The main results are as follows. First, within each transaction regime, both Stackelberg equilibria can be sustained as subgame-perfect equilibria (SPEs). Second, the Stackelberg equilibrium with the large region as leader is selected by the risk-dominance criterion. Third, the selected timing structure affects the critical values that define the transaction regimes. In particular, the large-region-leader Stackelberg equilibrium generates a larger tax-rate differential than the simultaneous-move Nash equilibrium, thereby shifting upward the critical values defining the intermediate regime in which brick-and-mortar and online purchases coexist. These results suggest that simultaneous tax setting should not be treated as the only natural benchmark in commodity tax competition models with e-commerce.

title: Attrition-Aware Causal Inference with GPS Tracking Data: A Study of Germany's 9-Euro-Ticket

detail.title: Attrition-Aware Causal Inference with GPS Tracking Data: A Study of Germany's 9-Euro-Ticket

declarations.funderStatement: Daniel Hörcher acknowledges funding from the National Research, Development and Innovation Office of Hungary (NKFIH), under Excellence24 grant #151498.

detail.abstract: Germany's 9-Euro-Ticket, implemented from June to August 2022, attracted international attention because of both the magnitude of the fare discount and its nationwide coverage. It sparked debate over whether the policy mainly generated additional public transport demand or shifted travel away from private cars. This paper estimates the causal impact of the policy on travel behaviour using a longitudinal smartphone-based GPS panel covering May to August 2022. GPS data provide rich, high-frequency, userlevel information on trips, mode use, and distance travelled, but they also pose challenges for causal inference: some users stop contributing data, observations are not continuously recorded over time, and some outcomes may be observed selectively in ways related to travel behaviour, which can bias our estimates of behavioural responses. To address this, we develop an estimation framework that treats panel dropout and selective outcome observation as part of the measurement process. The approach combines stabilised inverse-probability weights on a balanced user-time panel with a sharp regression discontinuity in time design. Applied to the 9-Euro-Ticket, we find that the number and distance of public transport trips increased substantially, while the limited magnitude and temporal mismatch of the reduction in car use provide little evidence of mode shift.

title: The Delegation Gap: The Disposition Effect and Other People's Money
affiliations: EDHEC Business School

detail.title: The Delegation Gap: The Disposition Effect and Other People's Money
detail.abstract: Using a unique dataset, this paper documents a "delegation gap" in investor trades - the disposition effect is reduced when investment decisions are fully delegated to an investment manager compared to when decisions are made by the account owner. The delegation gap is present in both retail and professional accounts, as well as when comparing trades made by investment managers on behalf of clients to those they made in their own personal accounts. The delegation gap varies across investor demographic groups and is positively related to economic news sentiment, suggesting a larger benefit to delegation during periods of negative sentiment. The evidence is consistent with the view that under certain conditions, delegating investment decisions can reduce behavioral mistakes made by investors trading emotionally with their own money.

title: Resolving the Israeli-Palestinian Conflict

detail.title: Resolving the Israeli-Palestinian Conflict

detail.abstract:
This book analyses more than three decades of peace negotiations between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO), from the inception of the Oslo process in 1993 to the present. It does not attempt to provide an exhaustive historical record of every negotiation. Instead, it seeks to explain why the peace process has failed so repeatedly and what can be done differently. The study pays particular attention to the roles of third-party mediators, the conditions for successful negotiations, and the lessons learned from critical junctures such as Oslo, Camp David, and the Abbas–Olmert talks.

This research project, in the fields of diplomacy, IR, peace and conflict resolution, aims to: (1) develop a comprehensive theoretical framework of conflict resolution; (2) apply it for a detailed analysis of peace mediation, facilitation and negotiations between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO), from the start of the Oslo process in 1993 until today; (3) provide original insights to explain the main peace junctions between the two parties; (4) outline the keys to successful negotiations, mediation and facilitation, so that, in the event that an opportunity for peace presents itself, the opportunity will not be missed; and (5) map possible solutions to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. The project explains the keys to future successful negotiations.

detail.title: Media Ownership, Newsroom Independence, and President Trump's War on the Press
detail.abstract:
Media ownership is now both directly and indirectly at the center of the Trump Administration's press-control strategy. With the deployment of censorship efforts and lawsuits aimed at press owners critical of the President, the regulatory activities of a Trump-aligned Federal Communications Commission (FCC), the grant of benefits to politically partisan, pro-Trump media owners, the defunding of public media, the adoption of multiple hurdles to independent newsgathering, and the involvement of the President in the joint venture to spin off an American TikTok, the Trump Administration has been systematically engaging in a multi-pronged scheme of press control by proxy, focused on ownership.

Today's media ecosystem is complex, with news outlets reflecting a range of ownership patterns with varying characteristics, legal rules, and owner incentives. In theory, such a mix could generate a range of owner responses to government pressure. However, if the Administration strategically continues to tailor governmental sticks and carrots to the characteristics and vulnerabilities of the various forms of ownership-and particularly while permitting increased media consolidation-it is realistic to expect more capitulation than resistance from media owners in response. 

Although there is no way to insulate the press completely from the threat of ownership-focused control, this Essay makes five recommendations to reduce the press function's exposure to proxy censorship: (1) exacting scrutiny of proposed media mergers and acquisitions from the vantage point of their impact on concentration in the market for news production; (2) constraints on FCC Chairman Carr's sweeping and politicized expansions of Commission intrusions into content; (3) rejection of proposed expansions of corporate boards' fiduciary duties of oversight to news units; (4) a skeptical review of the statutory compliance of the new TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC; and (5) development of funding models that would materially promote the work of journalistically-trained independent "evidence-based creators.

detail.abstract:
This chapter addresses the increasingly important question whether artificial intelligence (AI) may fulfill the dreams of its proponents and begin to solve the real problems of resource scarcity, particularly of affordable new drugs. Leaders in the AI community have floated the idea that artificial general intelligence (AGI) will change the world to one where individuals will contemplate what to do when freed from the demands of labor because resource utilization will be maximized.  We will live in an era of abundance. The same leaders have suggested that AI and/or AGI will tackle human biology and potentially find cures for all diseases. 

It seems almost certain that AI and/or AGI will be successful in establishing a much better understanding of human biology and ways to modify it to promote health. It is unlikely that intellectual property rules will play a material role in determining the path forward. Yet IP rules may help to determine the speed and scale at which the public has access to the benefits of the new technologies, and as always with IP there are risks of under-protection and overprotection that need to be balanced. As has been the case in previous iterations of challenge to conventional IP rules, there will be choices between stepwise adaptation of existing rules and the adoption of sui generis rules to address the changed environment.

We proceed in two steps. The first is to consider the issues raised by introducing AI generated inventions into conventional IP systems, most prominently patent systems. The second is to contemplate the possibility of new paradigms that are developed on a fresh slate based on evolving requirements, and not looking back on the conventional modalities.

title: Genes, Laws, and Marriage: ADHD Polygenic Scores and Divorce in the United States

detail.title: Genes, Laws, and Marriage: ADHD Polygenic Scores and Divorce in the United States
detail.abstract: Nearly four in ten first marriages among older Americans end in divorce, and who divorces is far from random. Using the Health and Retirement Study, I show that a part of the difference is genetic, and that family law governs how much it matters. A one standard deviation increase in an individual's own genetic risk for ADHD raises the probability that their first marriage ends in divorce by about 3 percentage points, a 9% increase over the baseline rate of 35%. This gradient is stable across controls, survives Oster bounds for selection on unobservables, and is not a proxy for the genetics of low education. The gradient also interacts with the law. Exploiting the staggered adoption of unilateral divorce across U.S. states, I find it positive everywhere but significantly steeper where legal exit from marriage is easier. Moving across the interquartile range of exposure widens it by nearly a third of its baseline, and the amplification concentrates in cohorts that lived most of their lives under the reform. The moderation survives state-specific cohort trends, a wild cluster bootstrap, and randomization inference. Earlier work finds the average effect of unilateral divorce on the divorce rate small and short-lived. That muted average masks a sharp distributional one. The law changes no one's genes, but it changes how much they matter for whether a marriage lasts. Family law therefore carries distributional consequences that fall unevenly across the genetic distribution.

detail.abstract: The proliferation of autonomous Agentic AI in lodging revenue management introduces a critical governance failure: unconstrained pricing agents trigger algorithmic cascades during exogenous demand shocks, driving room rates below operational cost thresholds and destroying asset margins. Existing frameworks lack an immutable, cost-aware constraint layer translating balance sheet data into active agentic pricing floors. This study introduces and validates the Yield Equilibrium Protocol (YEP), a Governanceas-Code framework embedding dynamic cost-accounting constraints directly into the agentic reasoning loop via a four-layer meta-prompt engineering architecture. An agent-based simulation executing 10,000 independent iterations, parameterized on audited data from a luxury five-star coastal resort, demonstrates that governed agents achieved a 98.4 percent Constraint Adherence Rate versus 68.2 percent baseline, reduced drift detection latency by 87.3 percent, stabilised Gross Operating Profit Per Available Room at positive USD 18.60 versus negative USD 12.40, and delivered a 20.4 percentage-point post-crisis occupancy recovery advantage. title: Bridging Public and Private Markets: A Total Portfolio Risk Aggregation Framework Using Factor Proxies and Iman-Conover Rank-Correlated Copula

detail.abstract:
Institutional investors adopting a Total Portfolio Approach — including sovereign wealth funds, large pension funds, and asset managers — increasingly blend liquid public equities with illiquid private markets, frequently bypassing traditional fund structures in favor of direct asset investments. Yet standard risk aggregation frameworks systematically fail to capture true joint tail behavior: linear correlation assumptions underestimate cross-asset correlation during market stress, while the operating leverage embedded in direct private investments remains invisible to traditional models.

This paper proposes a unified, non-parametric risk aggregation framework designed for portfolios combining public equities and direct private investments — a structural gap that existing practitioner models have not adequately addressed. The framework operates in two stages. First, synthetic proxy series are engineered via bottom-up cash flow decomposition. Unlisted targets are separated into core revenue and cost drivers, mapped to pure-play public equities, and aggregated via EBITDA-weighted exposures. The Hamada equation is deployed to systematically unlever and relever these returns to the target's exact capital structure. This isolates localized operating variance from the idiosyncratic debt profiles of the proxy firms. Second, empirical return distributions are preserved through bootstrap resampling, with cross-asset dependence imposed via an Iman-Conover rank-correlated copula — decoupling rank-based dependence from parametric shape assumptions and retaining the fat-tailed reality of observed market returns.

Applied to a representative 70/30 public-private portfolio across a 50,000-year Monte Carlo simulation, comparison with a standard parametric framework reveals that normal distribution assumptions systematically overstate capital requirements by 4.4pp at 99% VaR and 6.1pp at 99% CVaR. Beyond this methodological finding, the framework demonstrates that private asset integration reduces 99% VaR by 2.5pp and 99% CVaR by 2.7pp relative to a public-only benchmark. Stress testing across the 2022 rates shock and the COVID-19 full-year regime confirms tail risk deterioration of 12-14pp at 99% CVaR, while a hypothetical contagion scenario imposing 0.85 uniform rank correlation quantifies the cost of complete diversification breakdown at 22.2pp. For institutions adopting a Total Portfolio Approach, these findings provide a quantitative foundation for capital efficiency analysis and tail risk integration that existing parametric and statistical approaches cannot deliver for portfolios containing direct private investments.

detail.abstract: Rolling-window factor models for the gold futures basis exhibit persistent coefficient sign-flipping: the DXY dollar index coefficient is positive in some periods and negative in others, with only 64% sign consistency over a decade. We show this instability is regime-dependent, not noise. Using a dual Hidden Markov Model framework-one classifying market risk conditions (VIX and DXY levels) and another classifying CFTC positioning regimes (commercial-led versus speculator-led)we identify market states in which factor signs become statistically consistent. In the Risk-Off/Commercial-Led regime, VIX sign consistency rises from 59% to 75% (bootstrap 95% CI excludes coin-toss; overlap-adjusted z-test p = 0.046). Critically, F-tests show no evidence that regimes alter mean coefficient magnitudes (p = 0.531), while Brown-Forsythe tests confirm that regimes significantly alter coefficient dispersion (p < 0.001 for both DXY and VIX). The regime effect operates on the temporal distribution of coefficient signs, not on coefficient levels-a second-moment effect that we directly measure, not merely infer. This framework adds interpretive value, informing practitioners when to trust factor attribution, without improving point forecasts.

detail.abstract: For much of the twentieth century, the federal Food and Drug Administration maintained its reputation as the preeminent regulatory agency, renowned for providing vigilant and scientifically rigorous oversight that ensured the safety and effectiveness of drugs and medical devices. But a former FDA commissioner recently lamented that "[t]he FDA as we've known it is finished." Many commentators have raised concerns that reductions in force will leave the Agency understaffed, that these shortages will prolong review times, and that the standards applied to premarket evaluations of medical products will allow unsafe and ineffective products to reach the market. But in the half-century since the modern medical device regulatory regime took effect, critics had already identified many of these same problems. Thus, while the new administration's policies will hobble FDA's ability to fulfill its mission of ensuring safety and effectiveness and of permitting, and even of fostering innovation, simply returning to the old status quo cannot be the goal. Reforming the framework under which FDA regulates medical products and reconstructing the networks of expertise that are currently being shredded will be necessary steps. detail.abstract: This study evaluates the economic viability of converting overhead electric distribution lines to underground in Consumers Energy’s service territory in Michigan in the U.S. The circuit-level benefit-cost analyses incorporate value streams focusing on reliability and resilience improvements and changes to utility system expenditures. The findings reveal that undergrounding can provide substantial net benefits, averaging approximately $300,000 per mile (1 mile = 1.61 km; $186,000 per km) with a benefit-cost ratio of 1.9. While higher capital expenditures drive costs, these are offset by reduced operational and power interruption costs. Two-thirds of total benefits arise from improved reliability and resilience during storm events, avoiding outage impacts and response activities. Over 70% of circuits show net positive returns from undergrounding, though outcomes vary widely. The top 10% of circuits deliver far higher returns, with an average net benefit of $1.5 million per mile and a benefit-cost ratio of 5.3. A targeted program focusing on one-mile projects across the 35 most cost-effective circuits could produce $98 million (95% CI: $34.3M to $211M) in net benefits and achieve a benefit-cost ratio of 8.5 (95% CI: 2.9 to 22)—without incurring utility system net costs. These results suggest that undergrounding can be economically justified when implemented selectively, underscoring the value of a data-driven approach to infrastructure resilience.

title: Interpretable Physics-Informed Residual Learning for Photovoltaic Power Forecasting: From Accuracy to Diagnostic Insight
affiliations: , ,  and

detail.title: Interpretable Physics-Informed Residual Learning for Photovoltaic Power Forecasting: From Accuracy to Diagnostic Insight
detail.abstract:
Accurate forecasting of photovoltaic power, while still respecting physical laws, plays a central role in today’s energy systems. It matters for grid stability, for market participation, and for the real deployment of digital twins. Purelydata-driven models often look impressive on paper—they reach low numerical errors—but they sometimes miss what truly governs the system. They may predict output at night, misjudge inverter clipping, or forget that heat changes performance.
Small details, yet crucial ones, that make these models unreliable when conditions shift.
To deal with that, our work develops a Physics-Informed Residual Neural Network (PINN-Residual) built upon a hybrid DC model. It combines PVWatts’ linear temperature correction with Huld’s logarithmic refinement for low-irradiance behavior.

Instead of forcing equations directly, the network learns two residual terms—multiplicative (δₐ) and additive (δᵦ)—that describe systematic gaps between the physical baseline and what sensors actually record. During training, a time-adaptive physics loss keeps those corrections from drifting too far, so the learning process stays consistent with the real plant’s dynamics.

When applied to the PVOD v1.0 dataset (stations 00, 04 and 08), the model achieved high numerical accuracy (R² ≈ 0.97–0.99) while improving physical realism and smoothness through time. More interestingly, the residuals themselves carry meaning: δₐ tends to trace gradual module aging, whereas δᵦ mirrors inverter or wiring losses. What begins as a predictor ends up behaving like a diagnostic tool—one that can explain why deviations appear, not just when.

Overall, the study supports physics-oriented residual learning as a dependable and interpretable path for renewable-energy forecasting. It offers an approach that remains practical for operations yet transparent enough to guide future digital-twin developments in photovoltaic plants.

title: Price Path Continuity and the Cross-Section of Cryptocurrency Returns

detail.title: Price Path Continuity and the Cross-Section of Cryptocurrency Returns
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether the continuity of past price trajectories predicts the cross-section of cryptocurrency returns. The Frog-in-the-Pan hypothesis argues that investors underreact more strongly when information arrives gradually rather than discretely. I extend this logic to cryptocurrency markets, where conventional cash-flow anchors are limited and price movements themselves play a central informational role. To measure the structure of return formation, I construct a short-term Rank-Weighted Price Path Continuity measure (PPC) using daily returns over the prior 14 days and apply it to a broad, survivorship-bias-mitigated cryptocurrency sample from January 2020 to April 2026. Weekly Fama-MacBeth regressions show that short-term past returns are reversal-like on average, but become increasingly predictive of continuation when they are accumulated through smoother, more continuous price paths. The effect is robust across alternative horizons, alternative continuity measures, size-exclusion samples, market states, abnormal-volume environments, and cryptocurrency-policy-uncertainty regimes. Overall, the evidence shows that the path of past returns contains incremental information about delayed price adjustment in cryptocurrency markets, consistent with limited-attention interpretations of the Frog-in-the-Pan hypothesis.
